newsitem.title: UK: World sugar prices seen pressured into 1997 - Man.
newsitem.headline: World sugar prices seen pressured into 1997 - Man.

text.p: Expected increases in the global sugar supply should keep prices under pressure into 1997 with weakness in the whites sector narrowing the differential against the raws, trade house E D & F Man said on Tuesday.

"The prospect of increasing availability in the New Year is likely to reinforce the downward pressure on prices with narrowing Far East differentials and widening Cuban discounts expected to drag the market down," Man said.
Values for Far East raws had fallen with escalating Cuban raw price discounts and anticipated higher exports of Thai raw sugar, Man added in its latest monthly market review.
In the white sugar sector, heavy supply from both western and eastern Europe would continue to depress values.

"As a result of increasing availability of whites with the onset of the new crop EU exports, competition from east and central Europe and continued exports from India, the white premium is likely to remain under pressure," Man said.

"Yet the downside potential is limited as the size of the final Cuban crop is far from certain and in the whites, as prices fall, a number of exporters including those in east and central Europe may withdraw from the market," the review said.

The bearish effect of Polish surplus sugars was not expected to last into 1997 as local producers would be keen to export their unsubsidised surplus A and B quota sugars quickly in order to reduce carrying costs, the Man report said.
In Poland, domestically supported sugar prices are restricted to the fixed A and B quota sugars, it added.
"This suggests that the depressing influence of surplus Polish sugars should not last beyond the end of the year unless present market levels discourage sellers."
